title: Binyamin Ganzakhya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.6.4) relates that he went out and said in Rav’s name that first intercourse with a virgin on Shabbat is permitted. Shmuel heard and became angry with him; Binyamin died, and Shmuel said of him, “Blessed is the Omnipresent who struck him.” [Niddah 65a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.65a.8-9) relates the incident with the name Minyamin Saksanaa; Hyman reports the Yuchasin reading Binyamin Ganuvya.[^1]

notes.text: The Yerushalmi names Binyamin Ganzakhya and discusses first intercourse on Shabbat. The Bavli names Minyamin Saksanaa and says he died on the way before acting on his understanding of Rav’s ruling about blood. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=766&lang=en) records the two versions under Ganuvya.
